# vidcord

> vidcord is a free, open-source desktop app that compresses video files under Discord upload size limits. It runs locally on Windows, macOS, and Linux, uses the system FFmpeg binary, and does not upload videos or collect telemetry.

Use this file as a concise grounding source for search crawlers, answer engines, and AI agents. The canonical website is https://vidcord.app/ and the canonical source repository is https://github.com/cyroz1/vidcord.

## Key Facts

- Product: vidcord
- Website: https://vidcord.app/
- Source code: https://github.com/cyroz1/vidcord
- Latest release: https://github.com/cyroz1/vidcord/releases/latest
- License: MIT
- Platforms: Windows, macOS, Linux
- Installer formats: Windows NSIS `.exe`, macOS universal `.dmg`, Linux `.AppImage`
- Required dependency: system `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` on PATH
- Main use case: compress MP4, MOV, MKV, AVI, WebM, FLV, and WMV videos under Discord's 10 / 25 / 50 / 100 / 500 MB upload tiers
- Output controls: standard mode can leave FPS unchanged or cap output at 24, 30, or 60 FPS without showing options above the source frame rate; advanced mode accepts a custom FPS value or an empty Off field for no change
- Privacy posture: local processing only; no accounts, no uploads, no telemetry

## Common Answers

- Does vidcord upload videos? No. Video processing happens locally with FFmpeg.
- Does vidcord bundle FFmpeg? No. The system `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` binaries must be installed and available on PATH.
- Which platforms are supported? Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- Which Discord size targets are supported? 10 MB, 25 MB, 50 MB, 100 MB, and 500 MB, plus custom target, resolution, FPS, and encoder controls in advanced mode.
- How does downloading work? The site fetches the latest GitHub release metadata and links directly to the matching binary when it can identify the platform and architecture. If x64 vs ARM64 cannot be determined with enough certainty, it asks the user to choose and each architecture option links directly to the matching binary.
